name: AV Sgr
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 15.41 days; its mean radius is 106.2 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AV Sgr: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 106.2 +/- 8.4 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 24, Name='AV Sgr', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 4875 +/- 153 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, AV Sgr: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 2452.7 +/- 198.3 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 1.267 +/- 0.078 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way, 106 times the Sun's width, that swells and shrinks every 15.4 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 106.2 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 2,453 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, AV Sgr: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4069645924308096512 (quality A), from 2012ApJ...748..107P; Gaia DR3 measures none
